script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- India: 3 aircraft carriers, jets & troops: Israel, US plan to attack Iran after midterms.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy: Russia strikes area between Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra and monastery with ballistic missile carrying cluster warhead.
- Africa: Ukraine: At least 9 people were killed in Russian attacks over the past 24 hours.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA

- Military Times, 3 hours ago: US Army long-range fires make a splash on the frontline with China.
The U.S. Army has been upgrading its missiles and rocket artillery, largely in response to China's missile arsenal.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Holness blasts ‘two-mouth people’, defends JCF.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 13 hours ago: Holness blasts ‘two-mouth people’, defends JCF.
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness yesterday launched a blistering attack on critics of law enforcement, blasting “two-mouth people” while declaring his unwavering support for the Jamaica Constabulary Force (JCF). Holness comments come amid public debate over last Friday’s deadly gun battle in Sligoville, St Catherine. Speaking at a handover ceremony for the East Palms housing development in Kingston Central, Holness said state intervention was bringing positive changes to inner-city communities.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Russian forces attacked a house in Zhytomyr Oblast with a strike drone on 22 October. Nine people, including two children, were injured in the strike.

The Defense Ministry said it intercepted 808 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Wednesday night and Thursday morning.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russians kill couple in Zaporizhzhia.
Russian forces attacked a house in Zaporizhzhia on 22 October, killing a 37-year-old man and a 38-year-old woman, local authorities have reported.

- Balkan Insight, 12 hours ago: Acquittal Fuels Doubts over Transfer of Bosnian War Crimes Cases to Serbia.
While a court in Bosnia and Herzegovina has sentenced 13 people to a combined total of more than 180 years in prison for the killing of Bosniak civilians in two villages during the 1992-95 war, the acquittal of two others by a court in Belgrade has raised further doubts about the merit of transferring war crimes cases from Sarajevo to Belgrade.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 13 hours ago: Sudan: 'Many Still Missing' As Abyei Market Drone Strike Toll Rises.
[Dabanga] Abyei -- The death toll from a drone strike on Amiet market in the disputed Abyei area between Sudan and South Sudan has risen from 73 to 153, local officials say, and is expected to grow, as many people are still listed as 'missing'. The attack on Monday also forced about 8,000 people to flee, prompting condemnation from the United Nations and the UK.

- Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, 14 hours ago: 3 aircraft carriers, jets & troops: Israel, US plan to attack Iran after midterms.
The United States and Israel are preparing for potential military strikes against Iran after the upcoming midterm elections. Iran has announced it will reveal a new weapon called the 'Father of All Bombs' as tensions rise. US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to discuss military options recently. Meanwhile, Iranian officials warn of severe responses if attacked, emphasizing improved missile capabilities.
- Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Iran claims 7 oil tankers damaged in Hormuz, warns strikes if US helps passage.
Seven oil tankers sustained damage in the Strait of Hormuz as a result of attacks and naval mines. Four of the tankers reportedly caught fire while transferring oil, creating significant challenges. Iranian authorities have warned of potential targeting of US bases if the situation escalates.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 7 hours ago: Minnesota court reverses $20,000 privacy award in driveway camera feud.
In Minnesota, a conflict brewed between two couples over a shared driveway and the removal of a tree. The Stahleys performed maintenance on the Rubys' land without consent, leading to a legal battle. Ultimately, the court awarded the Rubys $27,000, with $20,000 for invasion of privacy. However, the appeals court overturned the privacy ruling, necessitating further proceedings and adjusting the damages for tree removal.

- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police.

A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night.

- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash.
England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday. The 27-year-old captain rewrote the record books by racing to his double hundred in 114 balls, surpassing the previous mark of 117 deliveries set by India’s Shubman Gill. In the process, Brook also eclipsed England’s highest individual ODI score of 182, held by all-rounder Ben Stokes.

Durban has been a focus of months of protests against foreign nationals, with looting and violence erupting after an anti-migrant march in the city two weeks ago. But the alleged attack on Helen Haines has sent a chill down the collective spine Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast On Monday night, Georgie Purcell shared a statement on social media in support of Helen Haines, who earlier that day had been allegedly attacked by a constituent in her regional Victorian electorate. The Perth incident came days after the federal independent MP Helen Haines was hospitalised with severe injuries following an alleged attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta in Victoria on Monday.
- The Guardian - Australia, 13 hours ago: Helen Haines vigil sparks calls for greater safety for women in politics – video.
Hundreds of community members gathered in Wodonga on Wednesday night to show their support for the independent MP Helen Haines after Monday's alleged attack, with many expressing shock and asking: 'Why Helen?' Attendees praised Haines for her compassion, support for young people and ability to bring people together across political divides. One community member said Haines was reasonable, fair and considerate and 'listened to everybody'.
